Heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for the informant and learned Addl.P.P.
for the State.
2. The two appellants in these two appeals are seeking Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.663 of 2024(3) dt.04-10-2024 suspension of their sentence and release on bail during pendency of these appeals.

3. The appellants have been convicted and sentenced vide judgment and order dated 27.04.2024 and 01.05.2024 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Sheikhpura in connection with Session Trial No.19 of 2023 arising out of Sheikhpura Mahila P.S. Case No.16 of 2022 for the offence under Sections 376(D), 387, 341, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (in short 'IPC') and have been ordered to undergo a sentence of 20 years rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs.15,000/- each for the offence under Section 376(D) IPC and in default of payment of fine, they shall further undergo three months rigorous imprisonment.

entities.text: Sheikhpura Mahila P.S. Case No.16 of 2022
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: For brevity sake, the sentences awarded under other Sections of IPC are not being mentioned.
4. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the appellants is that they have committed rape upon the informant/victim.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the victim in this case has stated in the written application that she was a student of B.A.-1st Part in Mahila College, Sheikhpura and on the date of occurrence i.e. 13.12.2021, she was going to Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.663 of 2024(3)
dt.04-10-2024 collect her admit card of Alim Part-I from Biharisharif college.
She had left her house at 6.00 AM in the morning during the winter season, however, in course of investigation, no material could be collected that the victim girl was a student of Alim Part-I.

She has stated in her deposition which took place in the year 2023 that she had done her graduation from Sanjay Gandhi Mahila College, Sheikhpura but on the date of occurrence she had also registered herself in the graduation course of Urdu from Urdu Board and she can produce the paper.
The submission is that the fact that the prosecutrix had left her house at 6.00 AM for collecting the admit card has not been proved by any cogent evidence.

In the same year, she could not have been a student of two graduation courses and two different Boards and even though she claimed that she can produce the paper, she could not produce anything in this regard.
6. Learned counsel further submits that there is a very surprising aspect of this matter.
The victim has stated that for the first time rape had been committed upon her by five named accused persons on 13.12.2021 near the Government School, Bangalipar.
She did not disclose this occurrence to anyone.
No FIR was lodged for that.

7. The victim claimed that while committing rape the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.663 of 2024(3) dt.04-10-2024 accused persons had made her video and her physical as well as mental condition had gone weak and for this reason she was not going to her college being afraid that she may be murdered.

The falsity of her statement may be found from the fact that after the occurrence she continued with her college for next two years and passed out her graduation examination from Sheikhpura college itself.

The so-called video which was allegedly made by the accused persons has Chandan Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10715055/
2 never been found in the mobile phone of the accused and there is no evidence to this effect.
8. Learned counsel submits that it would appear from her deposition, paragraph '8' that the victim had lodged another case being Sheikhpura Mahila P.S. Case No.31 of 2022.

entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: Initially when she was asked that she had lodged two other cases, she denied the same but then she was shown the FIR of Mahila P.S. Case No.31 of 2022 in which she and her Mami had lodged the case, then the informant has stated that she and her Mami had lodged the said case because they were finding a lot of misgivings and rumours in the media that she and her Mami were indulged in wrong act.

9. Learned counsel submits that the immediate reason for lodging of the present FIR is the fact that there were a lot of news in the media about the wrong act being committed by the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.663 of 2024(3) dt.04-10-2024 victim and her Mami.

10. It is further submitted that the falsity of the statement of the victim girl may be found from the fact that even as she alleges rape having been committed by five named accused persons, she did not go to any doctor and there is no evidence that she was treated for that so-called rape.
11. It is pointed out that surprisingly on the very next day of the lodging of the FIR, she recorded her 164 Cr.P.C. statement in which she did not mention the name of any of the accused persons.
She claimed that 20 days ago one boy had called her over telephone by threatening her to make her video viral and when she went there she was raped.

Again about this occurrence, she had not reported to police and she has not named the said boy and it is apparent that in order to save her from the media reports about her wrong acts she has come out with these allegations.

In her statement before the learned Magistrate she claimed that she identified two boys and she further claimed that she can identify the others but in her deposition she has stated that prior to the occurrence she did not know Chandan and other accused persons and after lodging of the FIR she was seeing the accused persons only in the court.
During the period of investigation, no TIP was conducted to Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.663 of 2024(3) dt.04-10-2024 ensure the identification of the accused persons.

12. Learned counsel further submits that the medical examination of the victim was done on 26.04.2022 in which the doctor had not found any injury on her private part but from the overall findings, it would only appear that the sexual intercourse had been done.

She being an adult, the finding of doctor that sexual intercourse has been done with her would not be a proof that these accused persons had committed rape on her on 13.12.2021 particularly when she herself admits that there were media reports about her wrong acts.
13. Learned counsel for the informant as well as learned Addl.P.P. for the State have jointly opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and release of the appellants on bail.

It is submitted that even though there may by some discrepancies in the prosecution evidence, it would appear that the prosecutrix has supported her case and she has stated that on 13.12.2021, the named accused persons had committed rape upon her.

sentences.text: In course of hearing, this Court made some queries for a prima-facie view and in such queries, it has transpired that the victim was aged about 21 years as is evident from the records at the time of alleged occurrence and even Patna High Court CR.
though she has claimed to have been raped by five persons, she had not reported the occurrence to police and there is no evidence that she was ever treated by any doctor.

15. Having regard to the submissions noted hereinabove and the materials which we have gone into for forming a prima-facie view, we find, at this stage, that the victim has herself stated that the occurrence is of 13.12.2021 but she had lodged the case only on 25.04.2022.
Thus, the FIR has been lodged after more than four months, she had not reported the occurrence to anyone and had not even gone to any doctor if she had been a victim of a gang rape.

She has not been able to prove that she was a student of Urdu Board for graduation at the same time when she was graduating from Sanjay Gandhi Mahila College, Sheikhpura and in this connection her statement that on the date of occurrence, she had left her house at 6.00 AM in the morning has also not been proved even prima-facie, from her deposition it appears that the immediate cause for lodging of the FIR is the so-called media reports in which there were rumours that she and her Mami were being involved in committing wrong act, in the circumstances, we direct suspension of sentence and release of the appellants on bail, during pendency of these appeals, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/-(Rupees Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.663 of 2024(3) dt.04-10-2024 Twenty Five Thousand Only) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Sessions Judge, Sheikhpura in connection with Session Trial No.19 of 2023 arising out of Sheikhpura Mahila P.S. Case No.16 of 2022 16.

sentences.text: The fine, if any, imposed as a part of sentence shall remain suspended during pendency of these appeals.

17. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only prima- facie and tentative for the purpose of suspension of sentence and bail only which would not cause prejudice to the either parties.

18. List both the appeals for hearing on their turn.
(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J) ( Ashok Kumar Pandey, J) arvind/-
